summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on fraud/security, regulation.

articles.title: Toast aims to drive AI into dining
articles.description: Most restaurants don’t have time to leverage AI tools, Toast executives say, anticipating profit from helping operators reap efficiencies.

articles.title: Visa, Mastercard join another stablecoin group
articles.description: The card networks are keeping their options open with respect to stablecoin communities, locking arms with Circle on its latest effort.

articles.title: FIS seeks to sell parts of capital markets unit
articles.description: The banking and payments services company floated the plan to offload pieces of the business after sales declined for that segment.

articles.title: Trump backs card bill, again
articles.description: The president called card interchange fees a “ripoff” in a social media post backing the Republican co-sponsor of a bill aimed at reducing them.

articles.title: Western Union faces profit drop
articles.description: The cross-border payments company’s business has been hurt by U.S. immigration policies, forcing it to embark on a cost-cutting plan.

articles.title: Visa loses bid to dismiss porn lawsuit
articles.description: The card network must defend itself against a 2021 lawsuit related to sexual videos of underage minors that were posted on pornography sites.

articles.title: Visa to buy BioCatch for $2.4B
articles.description: The card network giant plans to scoop up the Israeli firm to strengthen its defenses in a fight against fraud fueled by artificial intelligence.

articles.title: From POS provider to fintech platform: Epos Now’s embedded finance journey
articles.description: See how Epos Now built a full fintech platform with Adyen to power 80k+ locations.
